hero_prop_criteria.center_of_focus: The story, a shot or a character's attention centres on the object.
hero_prop_criteria.high_frequency: The object is present in more than one scene/act.
hero_prop_criteria.transfer: The object passes between two characters.

scenes.heading: EXT. SABA ELIOR’S COURTYARD — LATE MORNING

hero_props.name: Yonah's small lunch
hero_props.description: Yonah’s bundle of five barley loaves and two fish. It is offered to Jesus, multiplied into abundant bread and fish for the crowd, and later gathered as leftovers; the changed/multiplied food is treated as the same story prop in transformed form.
hero_props.reason: This is the central miracle prop and thematic mirror for Miri’s cakes: a small, real lunch that becomes enough when given. It is repeatedly shown, discussed, handed over, multiplied, distributed, and gathered.

hero_props.name: Miri's cloth bundle of honey-date cakes
hero_props.description: Miri’s wrapped set of three honey-date cakes. The cakes are protected, refused, reflected on, then shared; the set diminishes as Miri gives from it.
hero_props.reason: This prop embodies Miri’s fear of not having enough and her eventual generosity. It is repeatedly handled, guarded, discussed, and finally given away/shared.

hero_props.name: Ima's linen basket
hero_props.description: The basket of folded linen Ima sends with Miri to Saba; it creates Miri’s errand and carries/obscures the cake bundle.
hero_props.reason: The linen basket motivates Miri’s trip to Saba, is physically handed to her, delivered to Saba, and recurs as Nim’s hiding/resting place.

hero_props.name: The miracle baskets
hero_props.description: The baskets used to hold, distribute, and gather the miraculously multiplied bread and fish, culminating in twelve full baskets of leftovers.
hero_props.reason: The baskets visually prove the miracle’s abundance, are handled by disciples and children, pass between characters, and become a repeated symbol of more-than-enough provision.

hero_props.name: The small story scroll
hero_props.description: Saba’s small scroll tied with a barley-colored cord and sealed with a loaf-and-two-fish mark. It opens the story world of the feeding miracle, then returns to a drawing of the loaves and fish.
hero_props.reason: The scroll is the magical/storytelling object that transports Miri into the biblical event and remains an important physical anchor before and after the vision.

appearances.evidence: draws down a small scroll tied with a cord

appearances.usage: The scroll remains glowing on its shelf as the episode closes.

hero_props.name: Tav's broken toy cart
hero_props.description: Tav’s small toy cart with a loose/broken wheel. It appears broken when Miri first withholds a cake, then becomes an object she helps repair after choosing generosity. The peg used in the repair is included as part of this repair prop set.
hero_props.reason: The toy cart marks Tav’s need and gives Miri a practical way to help beyond sharing cake. It recurs in the opening and resolution, with Nim contributing the peg for repair.

appearances.usage: Tav sits with the broken cart; its wobbling wheel visually reinforces his need/disappointment.
